- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.3) mid-period, model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to counteract mean reversion bias.
- When model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–15% if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 3 days of forecast horizon, adjust next 3 days downward if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% in final 5 days.
